questions.q: Acetone reacts with ethyl bromoacetate and zinc in benzene, followed by H₃O⁺. The product is:
questions.explain: The carbon that carried Br bonds to the carbonyl carbon, the C=O becomes C–OH and the ester is kept, giving (CH₃)₂C(OH)CH₂COOC₂H₅.

questions.q: Why is zinc used instead of magnesium with an α-halo ester in the Reformatsky reaction?
options: The zinc enolate is less basic and does not attack the ester group of another α-halo ester molecule
Zinc enolates are stronger bases than Grignard reagents
Magnesium does not react with alkyl halides
Zinc converts the ester into an acid chloride first
questions.explain: The mild zinc enolate adds selectively to the aldehyde or ketone C=O, whereas a Grignard-type reagent would also add to esters.

questions.q: The Reformatsky product of benzaldehyde with ethyl bromoacetate is heated to eliminate water. The product formed is:
questions.explain: The Reformatsky product is a β-hydroxy ester, and elimination of the β-OH gives an α,β-unsaturated ester; hydrolysis, not dehydration, would give the β-hydroxy acid.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT true of the Reformatsky reagent BrZnCH₂COOC₂H₅?
options: It is formed by insertion of zinc into the C–Br bond
It exists as a zinc enolate
It is a strong base that readily deprotonates enolisable ketones
It can also add to imines and nitriles
questions.explain: Zinc enolates are only weakly basic and hardly ever remove a proton from the carbonyl partner, which is why easily enolised substrates can be used.
